To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the induction of the benzo[a]Pyrene-3-methylcholanthrene-7-mono-oxygenases in cultured cells of rat and mouse origin is mediated by oxidation product(s) of histidine formed by excited states of oxygen.

the photochemical generation of singlet oxygen in the culture medium by riboflavin is a useful method of inducing cytochrome P450 and that the mechanism of induction is due to the formation of an oxidation product of histidine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of chemical carcinogenesis and the induction of drug-metabolising enzymes.
the mechanism of induction of cytochromes P-450 and P-448.
the induction of cytopharmacologically important enzymes by a wide range of inducers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photochemical generation of singlet oxygen in culture medium containing ribo-flavin induces benzo[a] pyrene-3-mo-oxygenase by the conversion of histidine to an oxidized form of the latter.
the induction of the benzo[a] pyrene-3-monomoxygenase in cell line derived from liver by singlet oxygen is mediated by the oxidation products of histidines.

the induction of the enzyme by singlet oxygen is mediated by the oxidation products of histidyl residues of proteins, and that the oxidation of the histidine residues of proteins by singlet oxygen may be a general mechanism for the induction of the P-450 system by a wide variety of inducers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing that singlet oxygen is an essential component of the mechanism of induction of cytochromes P-450 and P-420.
singlet oxygen can induce the mono-oxygenation of benzo[a]-pyrene in cell culture and that this induction is due to the formation of an oxidised histidine derivative.
the mild illumination of riboflavin in culture medium converts a physiological constituent into a compound which induces the mono-oxygenation of benzo[a]-pyrene and other substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the induction of cytosolic enzymes by singlet oxygen and its oxidation products is mediated by a stable compound, which is formed by the photochemical oxidation of histidine in the cell medium, and which is as effective as the classical inducers of cytochrome p450.

the induction of cytoplasmic enzymes by singlet oxygen is not due to direct activation by the excited state of oxygen but rather due to the oxidation by singlet oxygen of a component in the cell culture medium to a compound which then acts as an inducer.
a mild light exposure of a riboflavin containing medium can convert histidine into an inducer of benzo[a]-pyrene-3-monooxygenase in cultured cells.
